acceptanceCriteria: each listed lazy entry form resolves key -> module and selects only the specs passing that key, with a test per form
a non-exported const registry named by the declaration and read through a declared accessor resolves, or the spec records why it stays refused
NGI-V0 rows amended or added (new IDs checked for collisions); the issue is closed with the PR
body: GitHub #946 (owner, feature request on the #871 dialect, V1-1365). NGI-V0-008 accepts only X, ns.X, new X(), new ns.X() of a static import, so lazy entries are registry-key-unresolved (import()) or invisible (require(), see #945), and a non-exported const registry read through an exported accessor is refused. Request: an arrow entry whose body is new (require(S).X)(), new (require(S).default)(), require(S).X, or import(S).then(...) with S a closed string literal is an edge to S under the existing reverse-import rules; optionally accept a non-exported const registry when the declaration names it. Motivation: lazy registries cut median spec import closure ~270 -> ~175 files in one real suite.
title: impact: string-key-registry dialect resolves lazy loader entries (require()/import() inside an arrow) and accessor-read non-exported registries (GitHub #946)
